name: What happens if the pool has cracks or leaks before demolition?

mainEntity.name: Does a leaking or damaged pool change the demolition process or cost?
mainEntity.text: Does a leaking or damaged pool change the demolition process or cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A damaged pool can be easier in one sense because it already has structural issues, but leaks may also create hidden complications. If water has saturated surrounding soil, undermined the shell, or damaged nearby hardscape, the contractor may need to address those issues before backfilling. Cracks can also affect how the pool is drained and how debris is handled. The big concern is not the leak itself, but whether it has changed the site conditions around the pool. Homeowners should mention any chronic leaks, shifting, or prior patchwork during the estimate so the contractor can price the job accurately. If there is visible settlement or washout, more site preparation may be required than on a dry, stable pool.
acceptedAnswer.description: A cracked or leaking pool usually does not prevent demolition, but it can affect drainage, cleanup, and soil conditions. If water has saturated the area or undermined the shell, extra work may be needed before backfill can begin.
